title: Recording: Silly Love Songs by Wings | 1976
content:
Studio Two, Abbey Road Studios, London
Producer: Paul McCartney
Engineer: Peter Henderson

The third recording session for the Wings At The Speed Of Sound track ‘Silly Love Songs’ took place on 20 January 1976.

The introduction was recorded during this session. Similar to that of ‘Money’ by Pink Floyd, it involved four elements: a conga, sandpaper, metal being hit, and metal being scraped. That part of the song became known as “the robot on the front”.

Several vocal harmony parts were also recorded by Paul and Linda McCartney, Denny Laine, and Joe English, the latter singing falsetto.
